title: Evidence Retention & Escalation Playbook: Unified Compliance Orchestration
author: Asha Menon
content:
Overview:

This playbook codifies Redwood's cross-domain process for preserving, retrieving, and escalating compliance evidence across RBAC, audit logging, data residency, secure SDLC artifacts, and incident response records. Its purpose is to ensure legal, regulatory, and internal audit requests are satisfied within SLA while minimizing operational burden and preserving chain-of-custody.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments of Redwood Inference.
- Covers evidence types: access grants/changes, authorization exception approvals, structured audit logs, API request payloads (when required), config snapshots, build artifacts, and retention metadata.
- Excludes product telemetry used purely for feature analytics (handled by Analytics team retention policy).

Principles:
1) Single source of truth: Evidence must be produced or referenced from an authoritative store (Primary stores listed below).
2) Chain-of-custody: Every evidence export is logged with who exported it, why, and an integrity checksum.
3) Least privilege: Access to evidence retrieval workflows is gated by RBAC and break-glass requires two approvers.
4) Time-bounded SLAs: Evidence retrieval and escalation timelines are defined below.

Primary stores and owners:
- Audit logs: centralized ELK cluster -> owner: eng-platform/observability. Retention: hot 90d, cold 2 years (see table).
- Authn/Authz events: Authz stream (Kafka) + long-term S3 archive -> owner: security/auth.
- Build and SDLC artifacts: Artifacts bucket + CI metadata -> owner: eng-developer-experience.
- Private deployment evidence: Customer-specific evidence preserved in Customer Vault (KMS-wrapped) -> owner: eng-private-deployments + security.

Retention schedule (summary):
| Evidence type | Live retention | Archived retention | Minimum integrity check frequency | Retrieval SLA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Structured audit logs (index) | 90 days (hot) | 2 years (cold) | weekly | 24 hours for hot, 72 hours for cold |
| Authz / RBAC change events | 1 year | 7 years | daily | 48 hours |
| Build artifacts (release) | 1 year | 5 years | weekly | 72 hours |
| Incident forensic exports | 3 years | 7 years | immediate after export | 24 hours |

Access model and RBAC mapping:
- Roles of interest: security:auditor, security:incident-responders, infra:engineer, product:owner, legal:compliance-review.
- Role-to-action mapping (summary):
  - security:auditor -> read access to archived evidence bundles, query audit indices, request export.
  - security:incident-responders -> create forensic exports, invoke legal-hold.
  - infra:engineer -> create ad-hoc diagnostic exports (requires approval if exporting user data).
  - legal:compliance-review -> request evidence with justification; receives exports via secure ShareFile.

RBAC exception and risk acceptance workflow (summary):
1) Requestor opens an Authorization Exception (AE) via Gerrit-style change request in the Authorization Exceptions registry (service: auth-exceptions.redwood.internal).
2) AE must include: scope, duration (max 72 hours without escalation), business justification, rollback plan, and list of affected systems.
3) Reviewer roles: security (primary), service owner (secondary). For high-risk systems (payment, customer-data), Legal review is required.
4) Exception approvals are time-limited and automatically documented into Compliance Evidence Store with an exportable PDF.

Incident response evidence-preservation procedure (numbered steps):
1) Triage: Incident owner declares "evidence-preservation required" in PagerDuty incident with tag evidence:yes.
2) Proof-of-need: Incident owner records scope and retention period in the incident ticket.
3) Forensic export: Security runbook execs the forensic-export script (examples below) to snapshot audit indices, authz streams, and service configs.
4) Seal and checksum: Each export is stored in the Evidence Bucket with SHA256 checksum and a signed manifest.
5) Notification and logging: An evidence export triggers an immutable audit entry (audit.service -> /v1/exports) and an email to the named requestors.
6) Legal hold: If Legal triggers hold, the evidence object is flagged and retention timers stop; only Legal and security:forensics can remove the flag.

Forensic export examples (CLI snippets):
- Export audit index range (hot):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" https://observability.redwood.internal/api/export?index=audit-*&from=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z&to=2026-01-07T23:59:59Z -o audit-export-20260101-07.jsonl

- Archive to evidence bucket (KMS-wrapped):
  aws s3 cp audit-export-20260101-07.jsonl s3://evidence-bucket/exports/2026/01/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:alias/evidence

- Generate manifest and checksum:
  sha256sum audit-export-20260101-07.jsonl > audit-export-20260101-07.jsonl.sha256
  ./sign-manifest --key /opt/keys/evidence_signing_key.pem manifest.json

Evidence retrieval SLA and escalation matrix:
- Tier 1 (Audit log hot, RBAC change events within 90d): Retrieval target 24 hours. Owner: eng-platform. If missed > 24h -> auto-escalate to on-call (eng-platform) and Security manager.
- Tier 2 (Archived logs / cross-region): Retrieval target 72 hours. If missed > 72h -> escalate to Head of Security and Infra Ops.
- Tier 3 (Legal holds / cross-border evidence): Retrieval target 5 business days for initial collection; legal must be engaged immediately. Escalation path: Head of Security -> General Counsel.

Escalation contact table:
| Role | Primary contact | PagerDuty | Backup |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| eng-platform on-call | oncall@eng-platform.redwood | P1234 | oncall-backup@eng-platform.redwood |
| Security on-call | sec-oncall@redwood | P2345 | sec-backup@redwood |
| Legal (compliance) | compliance@redwood | P3456 | legal-backup@redwood |

Audit logging operational standards (key checks):
- Ingestion latency: 95th percentile < 30s for hot indices. Alert if > 60s for 5m.
- Index integrity: Weekly replays of random index segments with checksum validation. Failure -> create incident and hold exports.
- Access controls: Only service accounts listed in audit-iam allow export API. Human export requires two-person approval via the Export Approval Service (EAS).

Secure SDLC artifact handling:
- Release snapshots: Every production release must have a signed artifact bundle (SHA256) published to Artifacts S3 and linked to the release ticket.
- Reproducibility requirement: Security/QA can request a reproducible build; engineering must provide CI inputs and exact dependency graph within 5 business days.

Compliance evidence packaging format (standard):
- manifest.json (fields): evidence_id, created_by, created_at, evidence_type, time_range_start, time_range_end, checksum, signed_by, retention_until, legal_hold_flag
- payload: one or more files (jsonl, tar.gz) stored with server-side encryption.

Quality gates and audit checklist (pre-release to auditors):
- Evidence package successfully uploaded to Evidence Bucket and checksum verified.
- Chain-of-custody manifest signed by two approvers (security lead + service owner).
- Retrieval proof: simulated retrieval run documented (date, operator) within last 90 days.
- Retention labels present and verified (region tags, residency constraint flags).

Privacy and data-residency considerations:
- Customer data subject to residency constraints must not leave customer region. Evidence exports for those customers are placed in region-specific vaults; cross-region transfer requires written consent and Legal approval.
- Masking rules: PII fields must be redacted unless legal requires full payload; request must justify and be logged.

Playbook maintenance and reviews:
- This document owner: security (Asha Menon).
- Review cadence: quarterly by Security + eng-platform + Legal.
- Change process: Material changes require in_review status, reviewers listed, and a 7-day comment window before publishing.

Appendix: related commands, helpful scripts, and contact templates:
- Export approval template (EAS request):
  {
    "requester": "alice@redwood",
    "purpose": "Regulatory request: FIN-2026-723",
    "scope": "authz changes 2026-01-01..2026-01-07",
    "ttl_hours": 168
  }

- Sample legal-hold email template and required fields are stored at: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/legal-hold-templates

- FAQs and troubleshooting: common failures (S3 KMS permission errors, export timeouts, index mapping inconsistencies) and their mitigations are in the companion runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/audit-export-failures

End of document.
